tagline: Through the Fortymile goldfields and along the crest to Canada.
intro: The Taylor leaves the Alaska Highway at Tetlin Junction, eleven miles east of Tok, with the Alaska Range and the Mentasta Mountains in view. It is narrow and winding, and it heads north into the Fortymile mining district, where wagon trails had served the camps since the nineteenth century. The road itself came through in 1951.

At Jack Wade Junction the byway turns east onto the Top of the World Highway, named because it keeps to the crest of the hills and looks down on the valleys. Old mine workings show along the way to the border at Boundary.

moments.title: Chicken
moments.text: Local legend says the founders could not agree how to spell ptarmigan, but the likelier source is nearby Chicken Creek, named, Josiah Spurr noted in 1896, for gold about the size of chicken feed.

moments.title: Jack Wade
moments.text: Claims on Jack Wade Creek have been worked since 1892, and in 1936 a whole bucket-line dredge was taken apart and hauled in by horses over the ice.

moments.title: Poker Creek–Little Gold Creek Border Crossing
moments.text: The northernmost border crossing in North America, where officers of both countries share one building and a line painted on the floor marks the border.

practical: Much of it gravel, with steep narrow grades and long distances between services. There is no winter maintenance, and the border crossing opens only in summer.
